questions.q: Hahnemann advised (§236) that in intermittent fevers the remedy is best given:
opts: at the height of the chill
immediately or very soon after the paroxysm ends
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. So that it can act before the next paroxysm.

questions.q: The concept of organ remedies (organopathy), derived from Rademacher, was developed in homoeopathy chiefly by:
questions.why: J. Compton Burnett popularised organ remedies, such as Ceanothus for the spleen and Chelidonium for the liver, building on Rademacher.

questions.q: Boenninghausen's 'Doctrine of Analogy' was used to:
opts: fill in missing parts of a symptom from analogous symptoms elsewhere
questions.why: Topic 4, Repertory. A missing modality could be taken from another location.

questions.q: The functional residual capacity is the sum of:
questions.why: FRC is the air left in the lungs at the end of a quiet expiration: ERV + RV (about 2.3–2.5 L).

questions.q: Hahnemann's 'Fragmenta de viribus medicamentorum positivis' (1805), the first collection of provings, contained:
questions.why: Fragmenta de viribus (1805), written in Latin, recorded the provings of 27 drugs.

questions.q: In the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules, 1945, 'homoeopathic medicines' are defined in Rule:
questions.why: Rule 2(dd) defines homoeopathic medicines; Rule 30AA deals with import and Rule 67A with sale.

questions.q: The continuous fluxion method of preparing high potencies is associated with:
Diseases kept up by avoidable noxious influences such as poor diet or bad habits, which disappear when these are corrected, are called by Hahnemann:
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. Not true miasmatic diseases.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the seven sections of Boenninghausen's Therapeutic Pocket Book?
questions.why: TPB's sections are mind, parts of the body, sensations and complaints, sleep and dreams, fever, aggravations and ameliorations, and relationship; it has no disease section.

questions.q: Fibrinoid necrosis of arteriolar walls is characteristic of:
questions.why: Fibrinoid necrosis is seen in immune-mediated vasculitis and in malignant hypertension, where fibrin leaks into damaged arteriolar walls.
